title: Overlaps & Triggers 🔔
description: Build interactive volumes that fire events without blocking movement.

slides.title: Trigger Volumes 🚪
slides.content:
# Invisible Event Zones

A **Trigger** is an actor with collision set to overlap only. When another actor enters, it fires **Overlap Events**.

Common triggers:
* **Box Trigger** – rectangular area
* **Sphere Trigger** – spherical zone
* **Capsule Trigger** – pill‑shaped

Place them via Place Actors → Volumes → Trigger Volume, or add a **Box Collision** component to any Blueprint.

quizData.question: A trigger volume blocks player movement.
quizData.explanation: Triggers have collision responses set to Overlap, so actors pass through but events fire.

slides.title: Overlap Events in Blueprints 📡
slides.content:
## Detecting Entry and Exit

In any Blueprint with a collision component (or a Trigger actor), add these events:

* **OnComponentBeginOverlap** – fires when another actor enters
* **OnComponentEndOverlap** – fires when an actor leaves

Both provide **Other Actor** and **Other Component** references. Use them to open doors, play sounds, damage players, etc.

quizData.question: Which event fires when an actor leaves a trigger?
quizData.explanation: EndOverlap fires when the actor exits the volume.

slides.title: Example: Door Opener 🔓
slides.content:
## Simple Script

1. Create a **Box Collision** component in a door Blueprint.
2. Set its Collision Preset to **Trigger**.
3. On **OnComponentBeginOverlap**, call a Timeline or Set Relative Rotation to open the door.
4. On **OnComponentEndOverlap**, reverse the action.
5. Use a **Cast To ThirdPersonCharacter** node if you want only the player to trigger.

This decouples the door from the switch; just approach and it opens.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use Tags for Filtering

Instead of casting, you can check if the overlapping actor has an **Actor Tag**. Faster and more flexible.
